newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli ship hit by Greek vessel, no casualties.
newsitem.headline: Israeli ship hit by Greek vessel, no casualties.

text.p: Zim Israel Navigation Co said its "Zim Pacific" container vessel, en route from Piraeus, Greece to Livorno, Italy, was hit by a cargo ship flying a Greek flag.
There are no casualties or damage to Zim Pacific's cargo. However, both vessels suffered damage, Zim said.
The Zim Pacific was at a distance of 10 hours sailing from Piraeus when the Greek ship's bow hit its port aft side.
"From early reports received at the company's headquarters it appears that the Greek vessel did not comply with international regulations for preventing collisions at sea," Zim said in a statement.
The Zim Pacific is making its way to Piraeus for repairs and the company is making preparations for delivery of the cargo to its destinations without delay.
Relevant authorities have been informed and the company has appointed an inquiry committee.

Zim, one of the world's largest container shipping companies, controls about 65 percent of the local cargo market. The government holds 48.6 percent of the company while the Israel Corp conglomerate owns 48.9 percent.
